thesis: Final IC view: retain the mechanical Compounder classification and NORMAL_CANDIDATE state. Microsoft’s moat, reinvestment runway, management and balance sheet are strong enough to justify a long-term position, but current price is above deterministic Base value and the AI infrastructure cycle leaves full-cycle incremental ROIC unproven. Approve a 2–4% strategic range, but start at 2–3% and use the 0.85 macro pacing multiplier; increase only after owner FCF/share and cloud margin validate the capex thesis.

evidence.claim: The aggregate score is 78.2/100, while score excluding valuation is 83.18, showing a strong business-quality profile dragged down primarily by valuation.
The mechanical archetype is Compounder because MT 87.0, RF 81.5, MA 84.25, FS 87.5 and EV 50.0 meet the configured Compounder thresholds.
All Hard Veto items are cleared after domain-owner and Red Team review, allowing the mechanical state to advance to NORMAL_CANDIDATE.
The locked DCF gives Bear/Base/Bull values of about $134.9/$441.3/$712.5 versus a frozen price of $497.75, so price is ~1.128x Base and still below Bull.
The Macro Overlay recommends a 0.85 risk-budget multiplier, indicating slower entry pacing without changing the company rating.

counterevidence: The strongest failure path is that AI demand remains high but accelerator/datacenter economics disappoint: capex and depreciation stay elevated, cloud gross margin does not recover, and owner FCF/share fails to compound.
EV is only 50 and the current price is above deterministic Base value, so a large portion of quality is already capitalized and multiple compression can offset operating success.
RF 81.5 is only modestly above the Compounder threshold and contains the run’s most important unresolved economic uncertainty: full-cycle incremental ROIC on the AI buildout.
AS 68.5 indicates resilience is stronger than power-law upside; this is not a high-convexity entry at the frozen price.
unknowns: Full-cycle incremental ROIC on the FY2025-27 AI infrastructure wave.
Steady-state maintenance capex and accelerator refresh burden.
Paid Copilot/agent renewal, expansion and workload-level gross margin.
Long-run terminal multiple if Microsoft’s growth rate normalizes at very large scale.
falsifiers: By FY2028-29 owner FCF/share fails to rise materially from the FY2026 capex-depressed anchor while AI capex remains structurally elevated.
Microsoft Cloud gross margin fails to stabilize/recover and Azure/AI gross-profit growth does not increasingly outpace sustaining capex and depreciation.
Commercial RPO ex-OpenAI, Azure growth and cross-suite monetization weaken together, indicating that current backlog and ecosystem strength are not converting into durable economics.

key_kpis.name: Owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: Material sustained improvement from the FY2026 ~$9 simple-FCF/share anchor

key_kpis.name: Microsoft Cloud gross margin
key_kpis.threshold: Stabilize and then improve as AI capacity utilization scales

key_kpis.name: AI/Azure gross profit versus sustaining capex
key_kpis.threshold: Gross-profit growth increasingly exceeds depreciation and replacement-capex growth
